Question Choices: A rigid transformation maps a segment of length 9 to its image. What is the image length?
Hints: Rigid transformations preserve distance.|The segment cannot stretch or shrink.
Solution: A rigid motion preserves the distance between the segment endpoints. The image length therefore equals the original length, 9.

Question Choices: A rigid transformation maps a 62-degree angle to its image. What is the image angle measure? Enter only the angle measure in degrees.
Hints: Rigid transformations preserve angle measures.|Turning or flipping does not change the opening of the angle.
Solution: Rigid motions preserve angle measure. The image angle has the same opening as the original, so it measures 62 degrees.

Question Choices: Select. Does a rigid transformation preserve area? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: The image has the same size and shape.|No scale factor other than 1 is applied.
Solution: Yes. A rigid motion preserves lengths and angles, so the image is congruent to the original. It covers the same area, although its position or orientation can change.

Question Choices: Select. Triangle ABC maps to triangle DEF with A -> D, B -> E, and C -> F. Which side corresponds to BC? ~~DF | EF | DE~~
Hints: Match each endpoint using the mapping.|B maps to E and C maps to F.
Solution: Track both endpoints: B maps to E and C maps to F. Thus BC corresponds to EF, also named FE.

Question Choices: Select. Triangle ABC maps to triangle DEF with A -> D, B -> E, and C -> F. Which angle corresponds to angle A? ~~Angle D | Angle E | Angle F~~
Hints: Use the first vertex mapping.|A maps directly to D.
Solution: An angle corresponds to the angle at its image vertex. Since A maps to D, angle A corresponds to angle D.

Question Choices: Select. Is a dilation with scale factor 3 a rigid transformation? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Rigid transformations preserve lengths.|This dilation triples every length.
Solution: No. A rigid transformation preserves every distance. Multiplying a positive length by 3 changes it, so this dilation is not rigid.

Question Choices: Select. A translation is followed by a rotation. Is the complete sequence rigid? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Each transformation in the sequence is rigid.|A composition of rigid transformations remains rigid.
Solution: Yes. Translation preserves distances and angles, and rotation preserves them again. Their composition therefore preserves those measures and is rigid.

Question Choices: Select. A reflection maps point P to P'. What can you conclude about the distance from P to the reflection line and from P' to the line? ~~They are unequal | Their relationship cannot be determined | They are equal~~
Hints: If P is off the mirror, the line perpendicularly bisects PP'.|If P lies on the mirror, it remains fixed.
Solution: Reflection pairs points at equal perpendicular distances from the mirror line. If P lies on the line, P stays fixed and both distances are zero.

Question Choices: Select. A rigid transformation maps one triangle exactly onto another. Are the triangles congruent? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Congruence can be defined by rigid motions.|The mapping preserves every corresponding measure.
Solution: Translations, rotations and reflections are rigid motions: they preserve size and shape. Mapping one complete figure exactly onto the other by a rigid motion or a sequence of them establishes congruence.

Question Choices: Select. A square is rotated 90 degrees about its center. Does its perimeter change? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Rotation preserves each side length.|The same four side lengths remain.
Solution: Each side length is unchanged under a rigid motion. Perimeter is the sum of these lengths, so it is unchanged.
